canonical_statement: The study asks how response-level task-verifier feedback should be combined with dense token-level on-policy distillation guidance for long-context reasoning when teacher preference and verified task outcomes disagree.

Teacher–verifier disagreement is diagnosed on fixed Qwen3-8B response sets from Multi-Table Extraction and High-Recall Retrieval, using eight responses per prompt and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 as the teacher.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The analysis covers 751 Multi-Table prompts and 2,908 High-Recall prompts across three prompt-length ranges below 64K tokens.

canonical_statement: Trajectory-level OPD score is defined as the mean token-level OPD advantage across a response, avoiding direct scaling with response length.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Averaging avoids direct scaling with response length and summarizes the teacher’s mean support for the response relative to the frozen rollout policy.

canonical_statement: A task-specific verifier supplies a response-level reward that may be binary or graded, and teacher–verifier disagreement is assessed from within-group ordering conflicts between verifier reward and trajectory-level OPD score.
GC-OPD separately z-normalizes verifier rewards and trajectory-level OPD scores within each rollout group before comparing them.

GC-OPD defines a signed response-level disagreement residual as normalized verifier reward minus normalized trajectory-level OPD score, so the correction vanishes when the two normalized assessments coincide.

RACA allocates each response-level residual across tokens using a bounded positive credit derived from each token’s OPD advantage relative to its response mean; the allocation signal is explicitly not interpreted as token correctness or causal importance.
The final GC-OPD advantage preserves the original token-level OPD advantage and adds beta times RACA credit times the signed disagreement residual; beta=0 recovers vanilla OPD.

If verifier reward or trajectory-level OPD score has near-zero within-group standard deviation, the implemented residual is zero for the whole group and the update reduces to vanilla OPD for that group.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: If either group-level signal has negligible variation, the residual is zero and the update reduces to vanilla OPD.

canonical_statement: Given OPD advantages and verifier rewards already produced by the training pipeline, GC-OPD requires only group aggregation, normalization, and tokenwise transformations and adds no teacher or student forward pass.
The training subset contains 9,527 GoLongRL prompts of at most 32K tokens across nine task families; three verifier families are binary and six are graded.
All post-training methods use 100 optimization steps, batches of 32 prompts, eight responses per prompt, a 32,768-token prompt cap, and a 10,240-token training response cap.
Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B are used as student models in no-thinking mode and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 supplies teacher token log probabilities.
Evaluation uses DocMath, FRAMES, MRCR, CorpusQA, and LongBench v1 QA with up to 120,000 input tokens, 8,192 generated tokens, a 131,072-token serving context, and YaRN factor 4.
A shared residual coefficient beta=0.10 is selected for both model scales from a fixed 231-example High-Recall Retrieval holdout with no overlap with the 9,527 training examples.
The shared training configuration uses tau_G=tau_T=1e-6 as standard-deviation guards and clips final token advantages to [-10,10].
Each training run used eight 80-GB NVIDIA H800 or H100 GPUs with rollout tensor parallelism and actor/reference sequence parallelism set to 8.
For several evaluation components, semantic-equivalence judging uses Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 with a 32,768-token context and 2,048-token output cap.
For Multi-Table Extraction, pairwise teacher–verifier disagreement increased from 40.6% below 8K tokens to 64.0% at 32–64K tokens.

canonical_statement: The exact 32K-filtered training file had a median prompt length of 9,923 tokens, a 90th percentile of 26,940, and a maximum of 32,766.

The appendix audit rerolls a 17,265-token GoLongRL example with eight Qwen3-8B responses; the native label is B, and representative recalculations show a positive residual for a correct B response (+3.464102) and a negative residual for an incorrect D response (-1.154701). The paper explicitly treats this as an illustrative audit rather than additional quantitative evidence.
The prompt-length disagreement diagnostics use fixed responses and characterize signal disagreement; they do not establish a causal effect of context length or task type on downstream training gains.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Because the responses are fixed, the analysis characterizes signal disagreement rather than task-specific training gains or causal effects of task type or context length.

canonical_statement: The residual coefficient beta was selected on a 231-example holdout containing only the High-Recall Retrieval task family, limiting evidence that the selected coefficient is optimal across the heterogeneous downstream tasks.
The main controlled experiments cover only Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B students with one Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 teacher, so model-family and broader scale generalizability remain untested.

Daggered baseline rows implement each comparator’s principal training-signal mechanism under the shared setup and should not be interpreted as exact reproductions of the original methods’ complete experimental recipes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The comparisons should therefore be interpreted as controlled mechanism comparisons under a shared setup rather than exact reproductions of the original experimental recipes.

canonical_statement: Training prompts are capped at 32K tokens whereas evaluation accepts up to 120K input tokens; the results therefore demonstrate benchmark generalization beyond the training length range without separately validating the disagreement mechanism across the entire 120K range.
Some benchmark scores depend on semantic-equivalence judgments from Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, so reported performance partly depends on an LLM judge rather than exclusively deterministic scoring.

GC-OPD cannot apply verifier calibration within a rollout group when either verifier rewards or trajectory-level OPD scores have negligible within-group variation; those groups fall back to vanilla OPD.

The authors conclude that group-relative residual calibration can integrate response-level verifier outcomes with dense token-level OPD guidance, with residual calibration providing the main gain and RACA adding further improvement over uniform allocation.
The paper reports public code availability at https://github.com/SolereZhang/GC-OPD.
